Data¶
  • Eurostat tour_occ_nin2m: nights in hotels, holiday and short-stay accommodation and campsites (NACE 55.1–55.3); Europe = the 34 countries in the extract (EU-27, EFTA and the candidate countries North Macedonia, Albania and Serbia), NUTS-2 regions. Population and area: Eurostat demo_r_pjanaggr3 and reg_area3.
  • One base everywhere: every figure is the 2023–2024 average. Seasonality is measured on nights per day (month length removed). Where only one year is published (Utrecht, Zuid-Holland, Iceland), that year is used.
  • Full definitions and robustness checks: Stage 2 Indices.

# Region attributes (one row per region)
REG = lg.drop_duplicates("NUTSCode").set_index("NUTSCode")[[

# Monthly series: one row per region x guest group x year, the 12 months as columns
KEY = ["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry", "Year"]
M = lg[lg["Month"] != "Total"]
NPD = M.pivot_table(index=KEY, columns="Month", values="NightsPerDay").reindex(
    columns=MONTH_NAMES)  # nights per day
ANNUAL = lg[lg["Month"] == "Total"].set_index(KEY)["Value"]
FLAGS = M.assign(C=M["Flag"].eq("C"),
                 u=M["Flag"].eq("u")).groupby(KEY)[["C", "u"]].any()

# Colours, chart style, maps
INK, MUTED, GRIDC = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
COLOR = {"Domestic": "#2a78d6", "Foreign": "#eb6834", "Total": "#1baf7a"}

def style(ax, title, ylabel=None):
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=12)
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, color=MUTED)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines[["left", "bottom"]].set_color(MUTED)
    ax.tick_params(colors=MUTED)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRIDC, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


# Region outlines: Eurostat GISCO NUTS 2024 (1:20 million, ETRS89-LAEA), via Nuts2json - data/raw/geo/
def _rings(g):
    return [
        r for poly in (g["coordinates"] if g["type"] ==
                       "MultiPolygon" else [g["coordinates"]]) for r in poly
    ]


def _geom_path(g):
    verts, codes = [], []
    for ring in _rings(g):
        verts += ring + [ring[0]]
        codes += [Path.MOVETO
                  ] + [Path.LINETO] * (len(ring) - 1) + [Path.CLOSEPOLY]
    return Path(verts, codes)


def _centroid(g):
    """Centroid of the largest ring (the main land mass): where a region's circle is drawn."""
    best = None
    for ring in _rings(g):
        x, y = np.asarray(ring, float).T
        cross = x * np.roll(y, -1) - np.roll(x, -1) * y
        area = cross.sum() / 2
        if area != 0 and (best is None or abs(area) > abs(best[0])):
            best = (area, ((x + np.roll(x, -1)) * cross).sum() / (6 * area),
                    ((y + np.roll(y, -1)) * cross).sum() / (6 * area))
    return best[1], best[2]


_load = lambda f: json.load(open(f"data/raw/geo/{f}", encoding="utf-8"))[
    "features"]
_feat = _load("nutsrg_2.json")
MAP_REGIONS = {f["properties"]["id"]: _geom_path(f["geometry"]) for f in _feat}
MAP_CENTROID = {f["properties"]["id"]: _centroid(f["geometry"]) for f in _feat}
MAP_LAND = [_geom_path(f["geometry"]) for f in _load("cntrg.json")]
MAP_BORDERS = [
    line for f in _load("nutsbn_0.json") if f["properties"].get("co") == "F"
    for line in (f["geometry"]["coordinates"] if f["geometry"]["type"] ==
                 "MultiLineString" else [f["geometry"]["coordinates"]])
]
NODATA = "#c9cbd1"
GROUPS = {
    "All guests": "Total",
    "Foreign guests": "Foreign",
    "Domestic guests": "Domestic"
}
GROUPS2 = {
    "All guests": "Total",
    "Foreign guests": "Foreign"
}  # the two groups shown on maps


def magma(n, reverse=True):
    """n colours from magma without its near-black and near-white ends; reverse=True: darker = higher class."""
    cm = plt.cm.magma_r if reverse else plt.cm.magma
    return [
        matplotlib.colors.to_hex(c) for c in cm(
            np.linspace(0.12, 0.85, n) if reverse else np.
            linspace(0.15, 0.88, n))
    ]


def _draw(ax, colors, base=NODATA):
    ax.add_collection(
        PathCollection(MAP_LAND,
                       facecolor="#f1f1ef",
                       edgecolor="white",
                       lw=0.3,
                       zorder=1))
    ids = list(MAP_REGIONS)
    ax.add_collection(
        PathCollection([MAP_REGIONS[i] for i in ids],
                       facecolor=[
                           colors.get(i, base if i in REG.index else "#f1f1ef")
                           for i in ids
                       ],
                       edgecolor="white",
                       lw=0.25,
                       zorder=2))
    ax.add_collection(
        LineCollection(MAP_BORDERS, colors="white", lw=0.9, zorder=3))
    ax.set_xlim(1.85e6, 6.6e6)
    ax.set_ylim(0.9e6, 5.45e6)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")


def _off_map(codes):
    off = sorted(set(codes) - set(MAP_REGIONS))
    if off:
        print(
            f"not on the maps (Azores, Madeira, French overseas regions): {off}"
        )


def region_map(colors, legend, title, note=None):
    """One choropleth of NUTS-2 regions. colors: NUTSCode -> colour; legend: list of (label, colour). Grey = no data."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8.2), dpi=110)
    _draw(ax, colors)
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11)
    ax.legend(handles=[
        Patch(facecolor=c, edgecolor="none", label=l) for l, c in legend
    ] + [Patch(facecolor=NODATA, edgecolor="none", label="no data")],
              frameon=False,
              fontsize=8,
              loc="upper right",
              title=note,
              title_fontsize=8,
              alignment="left")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    _off_map(colors)


def _row_figure(n, title, legend, note, nodata=True):
    """Figure with n maps in a row and one legend below; returns the bottom margin the legend needs."""
    handles = [
        Patch(facecolor=c, edgecolor="none", label=l) for l, c in legend
    ] + ([Patch(facecolor=NODATA, edgecolor="none", label="no data")]
         if nodata else [])
    ncol = min(len(handles), 6)
    rows = -(-len(handles) // ncol)
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1,
                            n,
                            figsize=(5.6 * n, 6.0 + 0.25 * rows),
                            dpi=110)
    fig.suptitle(title, x=0.01, ha="left", color=INK, fontsize=12)
    fig.legend(handles=handles,
               loc="lower center",
               ncol=ncol,
               frameon=False,
               fontsize=8,
               title=note,
               title_fontsize=8)
    return fig, np.atleast_1d(axs), 0.05 + 0.035 * rows


def map_row(panels, legend, title, note, nodata=True):
    """Category maps side by side with one legend. panels: list of (subtitle, {NUTSCode: colour})."""
    fig, axs, bottom = _row_figure(len(panels), title, legend, note, nodata)
    shown = set()
    for ax, (sub, cols) in zip(axs, panels):
        _draw(ax, cols)
        ax.set_title(sub, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10)
        shown |= set(cols)
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, bottom, 1, 0.95))
    plt.show()
    _off_map(shown)


def binned_row(series, cuts, labels, title, note, reverse=True):
    """Maps side by side (dict subtitle -> Series) on one shared scale, then the number of regions in each class."""
    cols = magma(len(labels), reverse)
    fig, axs, bottom = _row_figure(len(series), title, list(zip(labels, cols)),
                                   note)
    counts, shown = {}, set()
    for ax, (sub, s) in zip(axs, series.items()):
        cls = pd.cut(s.dropna(), cuts, labels=labels, right=False)
        _draw(ax, {k: cols[labels.index(v)] for k, v in cls.items()})
        ax.set_title(sub, loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10)
        counts[sub] = cls.value_counts().reindex(labels)
        shown |= set(cls.index)
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, bottom, 1, 0.95))
    plt.show()
    _off_map(shown)
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(counts).fillna(0)
    fig2, axs2 = plt.subplots(1, len(series), figsize=(5.6 * len(series), 0.3 * len(labels) + 1.3), dpi=110, sharex=True)
    y0 = np.arange(len(labels))[::-1]
    for ax2, sub in zip(np.atleast_1d(axs2), series):
        ax2.barh(y0, cnt[sub], color=cols, height=0.7)
        for y_, v in zip(y0, cnt[sub]):
            ax2.text(v + 0.5, y_, f"{v:.0f}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=MUTED)
        ax2.set_yticks(y0, labels)
        style(ax2, f"{sub}: regions by class")
        ax2.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
        ax2.grid(axis="x", color=GRIDC, lw=0.8)
        ax2.set_xlabel("NUTS-2 regions", color=MUTED)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def top_table(series, fmt):
    """Top 10 regions of each series (dict subtitle -> Series), side by side."""
    out = {}
    for sub, s in series.items():
        t = s.dropna().nlargest(10)
        out[sub] = [
            f"{REG.at[k, 'Region'][:30]} ({fmt(v)})" for k, v in t.items()
        ]
    display(pd.DataFrame(out, index=pd.RangeIndex(1, 11, name="rank")))

# Usable series: 12 published months, none confidential, at least 100,000 nights a year (details in the Appendix)
MIN_NIGHTS = 100_000
complete = NPD.notna().all(axis=1)
confidential = FLAGS["C"].reindex(NPD.index, fill_value=False)
big_enough = ANNUAL.reindex(NPD.index) >= MIN_NIGHTS
USABLE = complete & ~confidential & big_enough
LOWREL = FLAGS["u"].reindex(USABLE.index, fill_value=False)[USABLE].groupby(
    level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).any()
NIGHTS_AVG = ANNUAL.reindex(NPD.index)[USABLE].groupby(
    level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).mean()  # average annual nights

1. Tourism volume, intensity and density¶

↑ Contents

Measures¶

Nights spent = nights in tourist accommodation a year, average of 2023 and 2024 (Eurostat's annual totals).

Foreign share = foreign nights ÷ all nights × 100, over 2023 and 2024 together. Groups: mainly domestic under 40%, mixed 40–70%, mainly foreign 70% or more.

Tourism intensity = nights a year ÷ residents (average population of 2023 and 2024). Read: 5 = five nights in tourist accommodation for every resident, over the year. Counts only rented accommodation (no day visitors, second homes or stays with friends), so it understates the real pressure.

Tourism density = nights a year ÷ area in km². Read: 1,000 = 1,000 nights a year on every km²; ÷ 365 days ≈ 2.7 guests per km² on an average night.

A_ = ANNUAL.groupby(level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).mean().unstack(
    "ResidenceCountry")  # average annual nights
VOL = A_[A_.index.map(REG["NUTSLevel"]) == 2]
PPL = POP.groupby(level="NUTSCode").mean()  # average population
A0 = A_[A_.index.map(REG["NUTSLevel"]) == 0]
EUROPE = pd.DataFrame({
    "nights (m)":
    A0.sum() / 1e6,
    "per inhabitant":
    A0.sum() / PPL.reindex(A0.index).sum(),
    "per km²":
    A0[REG.loc[A0.index, "AreaKm2"].notna()].sum() /
    REG.loc[A0.index, "AreaKm2"].sum()
})
print(
    "Europe (34 countries; per km² without Serbia, which has no published area):"
)
display(
    EUROPE.reindex(["Total", "Foreign",
                    "Domestic"]).rename(index={
                        "Total": "All guests"
                    }).round(1))

Which demand dominates: domestic or foreign?¶

In [5]:
FG = ["Mainly domestic", "Mixed", "Mainly foreign"]
ann = ANNUAL.unstack("ResidenceCountry")
c_ann = A0.copy()                                   # countries: average annual nights (Part 1, Measures)
c_ann.index = c_ann.index.map(REG["Country"])
c_ann["PrcForeign"] = 100 * c_ann["Foreign"] / c_ann["Total"]
print(
    f"Europe (34 countries), average 2023-2024: {c_ann['Total'].sum() / 1e6:,.0f} m nights a year, "
    f"of which foreign {c_ann['Foreign'].sum() / 1e6:,.0f} m ({100 * c_ann['Foreign'].sum() / c_ann['Total'].sum():.1f}%)"
)
print(
    f"Foreign guests are the majority in {(c_ann['PrcForeign'] >= 50).sum()} of {len(c_ann)} countries; "
    f"median country {c_ann['PrcForeign'].median():.0f}% foreign")
display((c_ann.assign(Foreign=lambda x: x["Foreign"] / 1e6,
                      Total=lambda x: x["Total"] / 1e6)[[
                          "Foreign", "Total", "PrcForeign"
                      ]].round(1).rename(
                          columns={
                              "Foreign": "foreign nights (m)",
                              "Total": "all nights (m)",
                              "PrcForeign": "foreign %"
                          }).sort_values("foreign %", ascending=False)))
print()
# NUTS-2 regions with a usable all-guest profile; nights = average of the usable years
s_ = ann.groupby(level="NUTSCode").sum()
reg = REG.loc[NUTS2].assign(PrcForeign=100 * s_["Foreign"] / s_["Total"])
reg["ForeignGroup"] = pd.Categorical(pd.cut(reg["PrcForeign"],
                                            [-np.inf, 40, 70, np.inf],
                                            right=False,
                                            labels=FG),
                                     categories=FG)
reg["Nights"] = NIGHTS_AVG.xs("Total",
                              level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(reg.index)
reg["ForeignNights"] = NIGHTS_AVG.xs(
    "Foreign", level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(reg.index)

grp = reg.groupby("ForeignGroup",
                  observed=False).agg(regions=("Region", "size"),
                                      all_nights=("Nights", "sum"),
                                      foreign_nights=("ForeignNights", "sum"))
grp["% of all nights"] = (100 * grp["all_nights"] /
                          grp["all_nights"].sum()).round(1)
grp["% of foreign nights"] = (100 * grp["foreign_nights"] /
                              grp["foreign_nights"].sum()).round(1)
print("NUTS-2 regions by foreign group (shares of the NUTS-2 total):")
display(grp[["regions", "% of all nights", "% of foreign nights"]])

2. How seasonal is Europe?¶

↑ Contents

Measures¶

Gini index - how unequally the nights are spread over the 12 months. Formula: twice the covariance between each month's nights per day and its rank (1 = quietest, 12 = busiest), divided by 12 × the average month. Read: 0 = every month equal; 0.917 = all nights in one month. Classes: Low (no clear season) under 0.15, Medium 0.15–0.33, High 0.33 or more.

Spread ratio = S_R ÷ Gini. S_R (Lo Magno, Ferrante & De Cantis 2017) is the least effort needed to make the year even by moving nights between months, where moving one month along the calendar costs 1 and December and January are neighbours. S_R is used only inside this ratio. Read: about 1 = one season; lower = the busy months are split into separate seasons (ski + summer ≈ 0.55). Classes: one season 0.9 or more; main + secondary season 0.6–0.9; two seasons under 0.6; no clear season when Gini is under 0.15.

Season75 - the number of busiest months that together hold 75% of the year's nights (per day). Read: 9 = an even year (any 9 months hold 75%); 3 = three months hold three quarters of the year. A whole number, so coarse: it is shown on the maps as an easy-to-read companion of the Gini index, not as a separate measure.

Timing effect and Gini decomposition - defined in the last part, where they are used.

Each region's year is its 2023–2024 average profile: the share of the year's nights per day in each month, averaged over the usable years so that neither year dominates.

In [9]:
def gini(y):
    """Gini index of 12 values: 2 cov(y, rank) / (12 mean)."""
    y = np.asarray(y, float)
    r = np.empty(12)
    r[np.argsort(y, kind="stable")] = np.arange(1, 13)
    return 2 * np.mean((y - y.mean()) * (r / 12 - (r / 12).mean())) / y.mean()


def s_r(y):
    """S_R: least effort to flatten the year, months on a circle."""
    y = np.asarray(y, float)
    d = np.cumsum(y - y.mean())
    return np.abs(d - np.median(d)).sum() / (3 * y.sum())


LOW, HIGH = 0.15, 0.33
GCLASS = ["Low", "Medium", "High"]
SEASONS = [
    "One season", "Main + secondary season", "Two seasons", "No clear season"
]

ok_ = NPD[USABLE.reindex(NPD.index, fill_value=False)]
PROF = ok_.div(ok_.sum(axis=1),
               axis=0).groupby(level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"
                                      ]).mean()  # 2023-2024 profile (shares)
FAC = 12 * PROF  # seasonal factors
NPD_AVG = ok_.groupby(
    level=["NUTSCode", "ResidenceCountry"]).mean()  # average nights per day

ix = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Gini": [gini(r) for r in PROF.to_numpy()],
        "SR": [s_r(r) for r in PROF.to_numpy()],
        "PeakMonth": PROF.idxmax(axis=1)
    },
    index=PROF.index)


def season75(y):
    """Number of busiest months holding 75% of the year."""
    v = np.sort(np.asarray(y, float))[::-1]
    return int(np.argmax(np.cumsum(v) >= 0.75 * v.sum() - 1e-12)) + 1


ix["Season75"] = [season75(r) for r in PROF.to_numpy()]
ix["SpreadRatio"] = ix["SR"] / ix["Gini"]
ix["GiniClass"] = pd.Categorical(pd.cut(ix["Gini"], [0, LOW, HIGH, 1.01],
                                        right=False,
                                        labels=GCLASS),
                                 categories=GCLASS)
ix["SeasonCount"] = pd.Categorical(np.select(
    [ix["Gini"] < LOW, ix["SpreadRatio"] >= 0.9, ix["SpreadRatio"] >= 0.6],
    ["No clear season", "One season", "Main + secondary season"],
    "Two seasons"),
                                   categories=SEASONS)
ix["Nights"] = NIGHTS_AVG
ix["LowReliability"] = LOWREL.reindex(ix.index).fillna(False).astype(bool)
ix = ix.join(REG, on="NUTSCode")
sel = lambda guest, level=2: ix.xs(guest, level="ResidenceCountry").loc[
    lambda x: x["NUTSLevel"] == level]
to, fo, do = sel("Total"), sel("Foreign"), sel("Domestic")
print(
    f"NUTS-2 regions with a usable 2023-2024 profile: all guests {len(to)}, foreign {len(fo)}, domestic {len(do)}"
)

NUTS-2 regions with a usable 2023-2024 profile: all guests 268, foreign 259, domestic 263

Regional seasonality: overview¶

Seasonal Gini Index¶

The table shows data for Europe as one destination: it adds up the nights of all 34 countries month by month and measures that single year. Because the total is weighted by nights and the largest destinations are summer destinations, it comes out more seasonal than the typical region. The typical region is the median of the regions' own Gini values. The maps show every region's Gini for all guests and foreign guests on a shared scale.

In [10]:

              == 0]
EUR = cty.groupby(level="ResidenceCountry").sum(
)  # Europe (34 countries): nights per day by month
EUR_G = pd.Series({g: gini(EUR.loc[g]) for g in EUR.index})
EUR_FAC = 12 * EUR.div(EUR.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

Season75: how many months hold three quarters of the year?¶

The same picture as the Gini maps, counted in months. Darker = fewer months = more seasonal. Follows the Gini index almost exactly (Spearman ρ −0.95 to −0.96).

Busiest month¶

The busiest month of the 2023–2024 profile (nights per day). Regions with no clear season (Gini under 0.15) are shown separately: their busiest month is barely above the others and changes with small fluctuations.

In [13]:
MCOL = {
    "May": "#e7a3d6",
    "June": "#AA4499",
    "July": "#CC6677",
    "August": "#DDCC77",
    "September": "#117733",
    "October": "#999933",
    "December": "#44AA99",
    "January": "#88CCEE",
    "February": "#332288",
    "March": "#b7d5ef"
}
OTHER, NOCLEAR = "#9b9a96", "#e8e6df"
peaks, panels = {}, []
for sub, g in GROUPS2.items():
    s_ = sel(g)
    pm = s_.loc[s_["GiniClass"] != "Low", "PeakMonth"]
    low = s_.index[s_["GiniClass"] == "Low"]
    peaks[sub] = pd.concat(
        [pm.value_counts(),
         pd.Series({"no clear season": len(low)})])
    panels.append((sub, {k: MCOL.get(v, OTHER)
                         for k, v in pm.items()} | {k: NOCLEAR
                                                    for k in low}))
present = [m for m in MCOL if any(m in v.index for v in peaks.values())]
other = any(m not in MCOL and m != "no clear season" for v in peaks.values()
            for m in v.index)
map_row(panels,
        [(m, MCOL[m])
         for m in present] + ([("other months", OTHER)] if other else []) +
        [("no clear season", NOCLEAR)], "Busiest month, 2023-2024",
        "Busiest month")
display(
    pd.DataFrame(peaks).fillna(0).astype(int).sort_values(
        "All guests", ascending=False).rename_axis("busiest month (regions)"))
print("Regions whose busiest month is not July or August for at least one guest group "
      "(— = July or August; No peak = no clear season; no data = series not usable):")
nja = pd.DataFrame({sub: sel(g)["PeakMonth"].where(sel(g)["GiniClass"] != "Low", "No peak") for sub, g in GROUPS2.items()})
nja = nja[nja.apply(lambda c: c.notna() & ~c.isin(["July", "August", "No peak"])).any(axis=1)]
display(nja.replace({"July": "—", "August": "—"}).fillna("no data").join(REG[["Region", "Country"]])
        .set_index(["Region", "Country"]).sort_index(level="Country"))

Most seasonal: coastal¶

Foreign season vs domestic¶

Are foreign guests more seasonal than domestic: Regions¶

The Gini index of foreign nights against that of domestic nights in the same region. A difference within ±0.01 (the smallest effect worth reporting, as for the timing effect below) counts as about the same.

In [16]:
cmp_n = pd.DataFrame({"G_D": do["Gini"], "G_F": fo["Gini"]}).dropna()
cmp = cmp_n.join(REG[["Region", "Country"]])
cmp["diff"] = cmp["G_F"] - cmp["G_D"]
CMP = ["Foreign more seasonal", "About the same", "Domestic more seasonal"]
CMPCOL = {
    "Foreign more seasonal": COLOR["Foreign"],
    "About the same": "#b9b8b3",
    "Domestic more seasonal": COLOR["Domestic"]
}
cmp["which"] = pd.Categorical(np.select(
    [cmp["diff"] > 0.01, cmp["diff"] < -0.01], [CMP[0], CMP[2]], CMP[1]),
                              categories=CMP)
display(cmp["which"].value_counts().reindex(CMP).rename("regions").to_frame())
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 6.2), dpi=110)
for c in CMP:
    m_ = cmp["which"] == c
    ax.scatter(cmp.loc[m_, "G_D"],
               cmp.loc[m_, "G_F"],
               s=18,
               color=CMPCOL[c],
               edgecolor="white",
               lw=0.4,
               label=f"{c} ({m_.sum()})")

Who comes when?¶

Do domestic and foreign guests peak in the same months?¶

Compared only where both guest groups have a clear season (Gini 0.15 or more): in a nearly flat year the busiest month is not meaningful.

In [19]:
both_ = do.index.intersection(fo.index)
clear = both_[(do.loc[both_, "Gini"] >= LOW) & (fo.loc[both_, "Gini"] >= LOW)]
print(f"Compared in {len(clear)} regions where both guest groups have a clear season.")


def top_months(guest):
    o = np.argsort(
        -PROF.xs(guest, level="ResidenceCountry").loc[clear].to_numpy(),
        axis=1,
        kind="stable")
    return o[:, 0], [frozenset(r[:2]) for r in o]


pk_d, t2_d = top_months("Domestic")
pk_f, t2_f = top_months("Foreign")

)

3. Foreign seasonal patterns¶

↑ Contents

One season or two? The spread ratio¶

The Gini index treats the months as an unordered set: a ski-and-summer region and a coastal region with the same busy and quiet months score the same, although the first has two short gaps and the second one long closure. The spread ratio tells them apart.

What seasonal patterns are there for foreigners?¶

Season pattern (the shape of the year), after Ferrante, Lo Magno & De Cantis (2018); the size is the Gini class and the length is Season75.

  1. A year with no clear season (Gini under 0.15) is Year-round: its shape is mostly noise.
  2. For the others only the shape is kept: each month's deviation from an average day (factor − 1), scaled to unit length.
  3. The foreign NUTS-2 profiles are grouped by Ward's hierarchical clustering; the number of groups (3–8) is the one with the best silhouette.
  4. Each group is named from its average profile: Winter + summer seasons if both December–February and July–August are above average, Winter season if only the winter is, otherwise Summer season. Groups with the same name are merged, and a group of fewer than 5 regions is folded into the nearest pattern.
  5. Every profile - foreign, domestic, all guests - takes the pattern of the nearest group average.

Summer seasons are not split into "short" and "long": the shapes form a continuum, and the length of the season is what Season75 measures.

In [21]:
PATTERNS = [
    "Summer season", "Winter + summer seasons", "Winter season", "Year-round"
]
PCOLOR = {
    "Summer season": "#eb6834",
    "Winter + summer seasons": "#2a78d6",
    "Winter season": "#6b4fbb",
    "Year-round": "#1baf7a"
}
MIN_GROUP = 5


def silhouette_values(D, labels):
    s = []
    for i in range(len(labels)):
        same = labels == labels[i]
        same[i] = False
        a = D[i, same].mean() if same.any() else 0.0
        b = min(D[i, labels == c].mean() for c in set(labels)
                if c != labels[i])
        s.append((b - a) / max(a, b))
    return np.array(s)


def name_of(c):
    if c[["December", "January", "February"]].mean() >= 1:
        return "Winter + summer seasons" if c[
            ["July", "August"]].mean() >= 1 else "Winter season"
    return "Summer season"


dev = FAC - 1
UNIT = dev.div(np.sqrt((dev**2).sum(axis=1)), axis=0)  # shape only
seasonal = ix["Gini"] >= LOW
base = [
    k for k in UNIT.index
    if k[1] == "Foreign" and REG.at[k[0], "NUTSLevel"] == 2 and seasonal[k]
]
Xb = UNIT.loc[base].to_numpy()
Zw, Db = linkage(Xb, method="ward"), squareform(pdist(Xb))
sil = {
    k: silhouette_values(Db, fcluster(Zw, k, "maxclust")).mean()
    for k in range(3, 9)
}
display(pd.Series(sil, name="mean silhouette").round(3).to_frame().T)
K_BEST = max(sil, key=sil.get)
groups = fcluster(Zw, K_BEST, "maxclust")
names_b = FAC.loc[base].groupby(groups).mean().apply(
    name_of, axis=1).reindex(groups).to_numpy()
small = [n for n in set(names_b) if (names_b == n).sum() < MIN_GROUP]
for n in small:
    print(
        f"'{n}' has only {(names_b == n).sum()} regions ({', '.join(REG.at[k[0], 'Region'] for k, m in zip(base, names_b) if m == n)}): "
        f"folded into the nearest pattern")
keep = ~np.isin(names_b, small)
centres = UNIT.loc[base][keep].groupby(names_b[keep]).mean()
nearest = ((UNIT[seasonal].to_numpy()[:, None, :] -
            centres.to_numpy()[None])**2).sum(axis=2).argmin(axis=1)
ix["SeasonPattern"] = pd.Categorical(pd.Series(
    centres.index[nearest],
    index=UNIT.index[seasonal]).reindex(ix.index).fillna("Year-round"),
                                     categories=PATTERNS)
to, fo, do = sel("Total"), sel("Foreign"), sel("Domestic")
final_b = ix.loc[base, "SeasonPattern"].astype(str).to_numpy()
sv = silhouette_values(Db, final_b) if len(set(final_b)) > 1 else np.array(
    [np.nan])
print(
    f"{K_BEST} Ward groups -> patterns {sorted(set(final_b))}; mean silhouette of the final patterns {np.nanmean(sv):.2f} "
    f"(> 0.5 strong, 0.25-0.5 reasonable, < 0.25 weak)")
display(
    pd.Series(sv).groupby(final_b).agg(
        ["size", "mean"]).round(2).rename(columns={"mean": "silhouette"}))

Year shape clustering and the S_R ÷ Gini ratio agree almost completely. One season and Summer season are the same regions, as well as year-round and no clear season. Also, every two seasons region has the winter + summer pattern. The only overlap is main + secondary season: it includes weaker winter + summer regions (Trento, Bolzano, Lapland, Sofia's region) and summer regions with a small second season (e.g. Kärnten, Drenthe, Extremadura).

Where both guest groups have a summer season (135 regions), the foreign season (Season75) is shorter in 74, the same length in 42 and longer in 19

With small series left out, the shapes separate clearly (silhouette 0.60, "strong"):

  • foreign demand has one summer season in 178 regions and winter + summer seasons in 17 (the Alps, the Czech, Slovak and Bulgarian mountains, northern Scandinavia and Finland, and Martinique); 64 have no clear season.
  • Summer seasons differ mainly in length, which Season75 measures: three quarters of foreign nights fall in 3–5 months in 44 summer regions and in 8 months in 61.
  • Domestic and foreign guests share a shape in 74% of regions; in 41 regions only foreign guests are seasonal, in 20 regions only domestic.
  • Where both have a summer season, the foreign season is shorter in 74 of 135 regions and longer in only 19.

Is there a typical geography for each pattern?¶

For each foreign season pattern: how often the regions of each pattern are predominantly coastal, island, inland-mountain or rural (50%+ of residents), city (50%+ of residents in cities) or the capital region, against all regions. Geography shares describe where residents live, not where guests stay.

In [25]:
def ols(y, X, groups):
    """Least squares with country-clustered standard errors and p-values from t with (countries - 1) df."""
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)
    b = XtX_inv @ X.T @ y
    u = y - X @ b
    g = pd.factorize(groups)[0]
    G, (n, k) = g.max() + 1, X.shape
    meat = sum(np.outer(X[g == i].T @ u[g == i], X[g == i].T @ u[g == i]) for i in range(G))
    se = np.sqrt(np.diag(XtX_inv @ meat @ XtX_inv) * G / (G - 1) * (n - 1) / (n - k))
    return b, se, 2 * stats.t.sf(np.abs(b / se), G - 1)

4. What would more foreign guests do?¶

↑ Contents

Foreign guests are more seasonal than domestic guests in most regions. What does that mean for the region's year as a whole? Would more foreign guests change its seasonality?

In [26]:
# Both guest groups usable in the same year: monthly nights per day, per year and averaged
DOM, FOR = NPD.xs("Domestic",
                  level="ResidenceCountry"), NPD.xs("Foreign",
                                                    level="ResidenceCountry")
ok = USABLE.xs("Domestic", level="ResidenceCountry") & USABLE.xs(
    "Foreign", level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(DOM.index, fill_value=False)
ok = ok[ok.index.get_level_values("NUTSCode").map(REG["NUTSLevel"]) == 2]
d_y, f_y = DOM.loc[ok[ok].index], FOR.loc[ok[ok].index]
d_avg, f_avg = d_y.groupby(level="NUTSCode").mean(), f_y.groupby(
    level="NUTSCode").mean()


def gini_corr(x, y):
    """Gini correlation of x with y: cov(x, rank of y) / cov(x, rank of x)."""
    rank = lambda v: np.argsort(np.argsort(v, kind="stable"), kind="stable"
                                ) + 1
    return np.cov(x, rank(y), bias=True)[0, 1] / np.cov(x, rank(x),
                                                        bias=True)[0, 1]


def decomposition(d, f):
    y = d + f
    S_F, G_F, G_D, G = f.sum() / y.sum(), gini(f), gini(d), gini(y)
    GC, GC_D = gini_corr(f, y), gini_corr(d, y)
    assert abs(G - ((1 - S_F) * GC_D * G_D +
                    S_F * GC * G_F)) < 1e-9  # the decomposition holds exactly
    return {
        "S_F": S_F,
        "G_F": G_F,
        "G_D": G_D,
        "G": G,
        "GiniCorrF": GC,
        "GiniCorrD": GC_D,
        "RME": S_F * (GC * G_F / G - 1)
    }


def timing_effect(d, f):
    return gini(d + f) - gini(d + f.sum() * d / d.sum())


fe = pd.DataFrame(
    [decomposition(d, f) for d, f in zip(d_avg.to_numpy(), f_avg.to_numpy())],
    index=d_avg.index)
fe["ShareNights"] = 100 * fe["S_F"]
fe["ShareSeasonality"] = 100 * fe["S_F"] * fe["GiniCorrF"] * fe["G_F"] / fe[
    "G"]  # foreign contribution to the region's Gini, %
fe = fe.join(reg[["Region", "Country", "PrcForeign", "ForeignGroup",
                  "Nights"]])
print(
    f"{len(fe)} NUTS-2 regions with both guest groups usable in the same year")

257 NUTS-2 regions with both guest groups usable in the same year

Current situation: does today's foreign timing sharpen or smooth the season?¶

Timing effect = Gini of all nights − Gini of (domestic nights + foreign nights spread like the domestic ones), on nights per day. Would the region's year be more or less seasonal if today's foreign guests came in the same months as domestic guests? Read: positive = today's foreign timing sharpens the season; negative = it smooths it. Sharpens / Smooths when the 2023–2024 effect is beyond ±0.01 Gini points and has the same sign in both years; otherwise No clear effect.

Effect per unit of foreign share = timing effect ÷ foreign share of nights. The timing effect moves only the foreign nights, so it grows with the foreign share almost by construction; dividing by the share shows how different foreign timing is from domestic timing.

    [timing_effect(d, f) for d, f in zip(d_y.to_numpy(), f_y.to_numpy())],
    index=d_y.index).unstack("Year")

More foreign guests: three outcomes¶

The region's Gini splits exactly into the contributions of domestic and foreign guests (Lerman & Yitzhaki 1985). For foreign guests: S_F (foreign share of the region's nights), G_F (Gini of foreign nights alone) and Γ_F (Gini correlation: how far foreign guests' busy months coincide with the region's).

Relative marginal effect RME = S_F × (Γ_F × G_F ÷ G − 1), where G is the region's Gini: the percentage change in the region's Gini when foreign nights grow by 1% in every month (more of today's foreign guests, with today's timing). Outcomes: Flatten - RME −0.02 or lower; Sharpen - +0.02 or higher; Little effect - in between, or the sign changes between 2023 and 2024 (Fernández-Morales, Cisneros-Martínez & McCabe 2016). The paper's split of flatten into "flatter" and "off-peak" demand is not stable in these data and is not used (Stage 2, R5).

The effect is tiny. Even with 50% more foreign nights in every month, the median region's Gini changes by +0.3 points (+0.003 on a scale that runs to 0.917); three quarters of regions move by less than one point and none by more than 3.6, so the curves before and after almost overlap. The direction is slight sharpening in 137 regions and slight flattening in 57; in 63 there is no difference, mostly because foreign guests are few.

Conclusions and limitations¶

↑ Contents

  1. Volumes. Europe records 3.1 billion nights a year in tourist accommodation, 47% of them by foreign guests. Both are concentrated: the largest 10% of regions hold 43% of all nights, and foreign nights cluster in a few island, coastal and Alpine regions.
  2. Intensity and density. Relative to residents, islands and mountains carry the heaviest load (over 100 nights per inhabitant on the Aegean and Ionian islands), almost entirely from foreign guests; relative to land, capitals and city regions lead.
  3. Season. Europe's tourist year is a summer, coastal, August phenomenon (Gini 0.24 for the 34 countries together; August 1.9 times an average day). Capitals are the least seasonal regions in most countries; 77 of 268 regions have no clear season at all. Season75 says the same in months and follows the Gini index almost exactly.
  4. Foreign vs domestic. Foreign demand is more seasonal than domestic demand in most regions (176 of 257) and countries (19 of 33). Croatia, Bulgaria, Greece and Albania have the most seasonal foreign demand; Serbia, Czechia, Romania and Poland the least. The gap is about the same for Europe as a whole and for the typical region (about 0.04 Gini points).
  5. One season or two. In the Alps and the Czech and Slovak mountains, foreign demand is split into a winter and a summer season: the Gini index shows how concentrated their demand is, but their off-season is two short gaps rather than one long closure (Austria 15th by Gini, 31st by S_R). Across regions, a larger inland-mountain share goes with a more split foreign season.
  6. Shapes. Foreign demand has one summer season in most regions and winter + summer seasons in the mountains; the shapes are clearly distinct. Summer seasons differ mainly in length, and foreign guests' summer is usually shorter than domestic guests'.
  7. What more foreign guests would do: very little. Even 50% more foreign nights in every month would move the median region's Gini by less than one point. The direction is slight sharpening in 137 regions and slight flattening in 57; in 63 there is no difference, mostly because foreign guests are few.
  8. Geography of the patterns. Year-round foreign demand is typical of cities and capitals, winter + summer seasons of mountain regions; summer-season regions look like Europe as a whole.

Limitations¶

  • Two years only (2023–2024). No pre-COVID baseline at NUTS-2 and no long-run change; the average reduces, but does not remove, one-off events (Easter falls in April 2023 and March 2024).
  • Establishments only. Countries may exclude establishments with fewer than 10 (in small countries 20) bed places, so small private rentals, often very seasonal, are under-counted, unevenly across countries. Intensity and density count only rented accommodation, so they understate the real pressure.
  • Volume floor. Monthly series under 100,000 nights a year are left out of the seasonality measures, because their Gini is unstable from year to year: the foreign series of Dytiki Makedonia, Ceuta, Melilla, Molise, Svalbard, Opolskie and Sud-Vest Oltenia, and the domestic series of Ceuta, Svalbard and Liechtenstein. Volumes, intensity and density still include them.
  • Gaps and flags. Utrecht, Zuid-Holland and Iceland have 2023 only. Guadeloupe, Guyane and Mayotte have no usable domestic and foreign monthly series (missing or confidential months). Corse and the overseas regions carry Eurostat's low-reliability flag; Albania's 2023 values are Eurostat estimates. Serbia has no published area (no density); Svalbard has no residents (no intensity).
  • Foreign guests are one group - the data have no countries of origin.
  • The marginal effect assumes more of today's foreign guests, growing by the same percentage in every month; new markets with other seasons are not covered. It is relative to the region's Gini, so in nearly flat regions a large RME is a small absolute change, and it is near 0 where foreign guests are almost all nights.
  • Geography shares describe residents, not where guests stay; climate, access, ski and beach supply and prices are not in the data.
  • Accounting comparisons and associations, not causal effects.

Appendix¶

↑ Contents

Which series are used¶

A series (one region, one guest group, one year) is used when all 12 months are published, none is confidential (Eurostat flag C) and it has at least 100,000 nights a year: below that size the Gini of a series moves several times more from one year to the next (Stage 2, A1). The table lists every series that fails the rule and why. Months flagged u (low reliability) are kept and marked LowReliability.

def _usable(guest):
    u = USABLE.xs(guest, level="ResidenceCountry")
    return set(u[u].index.get_level_values("NUTSCode")) & set(NUTS2)


_ud = USABLE.xs("Domestic", level="ResidenceCountry")
_both_ = _ud & USABLE.xs("Foreign", level="ResidenceCountry").reindex(_ud.index, fill_value=False)
_both = set(_both_[_both_].index.get_level_values("NUTSCode")) & set(NUTS2)
_vol = set(ANNUAL.xs("Total", level="ResidenceCountry").dropna().index.get_level_values("NUTSCode")) & set(NUTS2)
_pop = set(POP.groupby(level="NUTSCode").mean().dropna().index)
_area = set(REG["AreaKm2"].dropna().index)
_geo = set(REG.dropna(subset=["PrcCoastal", "PrcRural", "PrcIsland", "PrcInlandMountain"]).index)
SERIES_RULE = "monthly series incomplete, confidential or under 100,000 nights"
COVERAGE = [("1. Nights and foreign share", _vol, ""),
            ("1. Intensity (nights per inhabitant)", _vol & _pop, "no residents"),
            ("1. Density (nights per km²)", _vol & _area, "no published area"),
            ("2. Seasonality, all guests", _usable("Total"), SERIES_RULE),
            ("2-3. Seasonality and patterns, foreign guests", _usable("Foreign"), SERIES_RULE),
            ("2-4. Foreign vs domestic; foreign effect", _both, SERIES_RULE + " (either guest group)"),
            ("3. Typical geography of the patterns", _usable("Foreign") & _geo, "no geography data or no usable foreign series")]
MANY = 12
rows_ = []
for name, codes, why in COVERAGE:
    miss = sorted(set(NUTS2) - codes)
    left = "—" if not miss else (", ".join(REG.loc[miss, "Region"]) if len(miss) <= MANY else f"{len(miss)} regions: {why}")
    rows_.append({"part": name, "regions": len(codes), "not included": left})
with pd.option_context("display.max_colwidth", None):
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows_).set_index("part"))
